    Cluster decision paths

    Source: R/decision-path.R
    sdt_seq_cluster.Rd

    Groups casualties by how similar their board pathways are: an optimal matching dissimilarity between state sequences, then partitioning around medoids. What comes out is a small number of characteristic ways through the board, which is usually more useful than a per-casualty path listing.

    Usage

    sdt_seq_cluster(run, k = 3L, method = "OM", indel = 1, sm = "CONSTANT")

    Arguments

    run

    A game_run from sdt_simulate().

    k

    Number of clusters.

    method

    Dissimilarity passed to TraMineR::seqdist(). "OM" is optimal matching.

    indel

    Insertion/deletion cost for optimal matching.

    sm

    Substitution-cost matrix or method. "CONSTANT" applies a flat cost, the right default when no substitution is more plausible than another.

    Value

    A tibble::tibble() with one row per sequence: replication, id, cluster, and medoid, which flags the sequence representing its cluster.

    See also

    sdt_seqdef(), sdt_plot_sequences().

    Examples

    co <- sdt_synthetic_cohort(n = 30, seed = 1)
run <- sdt_simulate(sdt_scenario(co), replications = 2, seed = 1,
                    verbose = FALSE)
if (requireNamespace("TraMineR", quietly = TRUE) &&
    requireNamespace("WeightedCluster", quietly = TRUE)) {
  sdt_seq_cluster(run, k = 3)
}
